item.title: Congress Grapples with Potential $200-Billion Request from Pentagon for Iran Campaign
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - The Pentagon could ask Congress for 200-billion dollars to support their military efforts in Iran. Members are approaching this request with caution, wanting to take a good look at what the Pentagon is asking for before they give their approval.

item.title: Delta County makes headway on blizzard recovery
item.description: WZMQ 19 sat down with the Delta County Emergency Management coordinator to discuss blizzard response efforts.

item.title: Mullin DHS Nomination Advances Out of Committee After Key Democratic Vote
item.description: Sen. Markwayne Mullin’s, R-Okla., nomination cleared a key hurdle on Capitol Hill earlier today, advancing out of the Senate Homeland Security Committee in a razor-thin 8-to-7 vote.

item.title: Michigan leaders push new gun reforms as red flag law data shows hundreds of interventions
item.description: Michigan officials say the state’s red flag law is already preventing violence, citing hundreds of firearm removals in its first full year. Now, lawmakers and advocates are pushing a new package of gun safety bills aimed at expanding those protections.

item.title: Senate Showdown Intensifies Over SAVE America Act
item.description: It’s day three — and counting — of what’s shaping up to be a marathon debate in the U.S. Senate. Senators are digging in over the “SAVE America Act” and some of the controversial additions President Donald Trump wants to see included in the bill.

item.title: Campus organizations take part in third annual NMU Day of Giving
item.description: Northern Michigan University held its third annual Day of Giving on Thursday, as a 24-hour fundraising event for various needs. One campus organization in particular is tackling this year's initiative at a unique angle. The NMU Music Department is more focused on highlighting its strong community through alumni, employees, and parents and families.

item.title: Jazz Festival 2026 kicks off at Northern Michigan University
item.description: NMU's annual Jazz Festival returned Thursday, bringing in high school and middle school ensembles from 7 schools around the Upper Peninsula.

item.title: Marquette Mayor praises snow response
item.description: As we continue to clean up after the record-setting Saint Patrick's blizzard of 2026, communities across the U.P. are assessing the damage and taking stock of the toll the storm had on community resources.

item.title: Marquette hotel project scales back plans, no indoor parking structure
